value: Purely temporary in nature
reasoning: The classical school held that flexible wages, prices and interest rates, together with Say's law that supply creates its own demand, restore full employment automatically, so any unemployment is only a short-run departure that the market itself corrects.

value: More fixed capital per worker
reasoning: Capital deepening means raising the capital-labour ratio, that is equipping each worker with more capital, as distinct from capital widening, which adds capital only in step with a growing workforce.

value: The claim that Article 32 extends to enforcing ordinary law unconnected with fundamental rights
reasoning: Article 32 is a remedy confined to the enforcement of the rights conferred by Part III; a claim resting on ordinary law with no fundamental-rights element must be taken to a High Court under Article 226 or to the appropriate civil forum.

value: Habeas Corpus
reasoning: Habeas corpus, literally 'you may have the body', commands the detaining authority to produce the detained person before the court so that the legality of the detention can be examined, and it is released if the detention is unlawful.

value: To promote village and cottage industries
reasoning: Promotion of cottage industries is a Directive Principle addressed to the State, not a duty of the citizen; respecting the National Flag, defending the country and providing education to one's child between six and fourteen are all listed among the Fundamental Duties in Article 51A.

value: War, external aggression and armed rebellion
reasoning: The Forty-fourth Amendment replaced the vague expression 'internal disturbance' with 'armed rebellion' precisely to make a national emergency harder to proclaim, so the three surviving grounds are war, external aggression and armed rebellion.

value: The claim that relief lies only against a husband or male live-in partner
reasoning: The Act allows an aggrieved woman to proceed against any respondent with whom she has been in a domestic relationship, expressly including relatives of the husband or male partner, so the remedy is not confined to the husband or live-in partner alone.

value: The claim that NIIF and NIF are the same organisation
reasoning: The National Investment Fund, created in 2005, holds the proceeds of disinvestment of public sector undertakings, whereas the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund announced in the 2015-16 Budget is a separate vehicle raising money to finance infrastructure and operating through more than one alternative investment fund.

value: The claim that it was set up by the British in the Second World War
reasoning: The Andaman and Nicobar Command was raised in 2001 as independent India's first tri-service theatre command, with its headquarters at Port Blair under a three-star commander-in-chief drawn in rotation from the three Services.

value: The Service Chief who has served longest on the Committee
reasoning: The Chiefs of Staff Committee has no permanent head; by convention the chairmanship rotates and falls to whichever of the three Service Chiefs has been a member of the Committee for the longest time.

value: An infantry regiment of the Indian Army
reasoning: The Jammu and Kashmir Rifles trace their descent from the forces of the princely State of Jammu and Kashmir and were absorbed into the Indian Army after 1947 as a regular infantry regiment, distinct both from the Rashtriya Rifles and from the State armed police.

value: The Army has its own Corps of Air Defence
reasoning: Army Air Defence was carved out of the Regiment of Artillery in 1994 as a separate corps responsible for defending field formations against air attack; the Mechanised Infantry, the Corps of Electrical and Mechanical Engineers and the Army Medical and Dental Corps are likewise all distinct arms and services in their own right.

value: North Eastern Command
reasoning: The Indian Army has six operational commands, Northern, Southern, Eastern, Western, Central and South Western, together with the Army Training Command at Shimla; the north-east falls under Eastern Command and there is no separate North Eastern Command.

value: The rank of Second Lieutenant has been abolished
reasoning: Following the cadre review of the mid-2000s officers are commissioned directly in the rank of Lieutenant and the rank of Second Lieutenant is no longer conferred; the Chief of Army Staff holds the rank of General, and Lieutenant General is senior to Major General, so the other statements are wrong.

value: Tatra
reasoning: Tatra is a heavy all-terrain truck used to carry launchers and equipment, not a missile at all, whereas Akash and Trishul are surface-to-air missiles. Note that Astra is also arguably out of place here, being a beyond-visual-range air-to-air missile rather than a ground-based air-defence system, so the question has a second defensible answer.

value: The share of the services sector has increased sharply
reasoning: Services now contribute over half of India's gross value added, having risen steeply since the 1990s, while agriculture's share has fallen steadily and manufacturing's has stayed broadly flat rather than declining.

value: Foreign Portfolio Investment
reasoning: Hot money is capital that can be pulled out at short notice; portfolio investment in shares and bonds by foreign institutional investors is exactly that, unlike foreign direct investment, which is locked into physical assets and long-term control.

value: All of these — CRISIL, CARE and ICRA
reasoning: CRISIL, CARE and ICRA are all credit rating agencies registered with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, alongside others such as India Ratings and Brickwork.

value: Y. V. Reddy
reasoning: The Fourteenth Finance Commission, constituted in 2013 and reporting for the period 2015 to 2020, was chaired by the former Reserve Bank Governor Y. V. Reddy, and it raised the States' share of the divisible pool of central taxes to 42 per cent.

value: The United States, Canada and Mexico
reasoning: The North American Free Trade Agreement, in force from 1994, created a free-trade area comprising the United States, Canada and Mexico.

value: All three — Article 17, the 1955 Act and the 1989 Act
reasoning: Article 17 abolishes untouchability and forbids its practice, the Protection of Civil Rights Act of 1955 punishes the enforcement of any disability arising from it, and the Prevention of Atrocities Act of 1989 creates special offences and courts for crimes against Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

value: The claim that the Supreme Court alone may issue writs to protect fundamental rights
reasoning: High Courts also issue the same writs under Article 226, and their writ power is in fact wider because it extends beyond fundamental rights to any other legal right; the Supreme Court's writ jurisdiction under Article 32 is therefore concurrent, not exclusive.

value: Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram
reasoning: The Sixth Schedule provides for autonomous districts and autonomous district councils in the tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram; the tribal areas of other north-eastern States are not covered by it.

value: The claim that Ninth Schedule laws become void for violating a fundamental right
reasoning: Article 31B provides the opposite, that an Act placed in the Ninth Schedule shall not be deemed void merely because it takes away or abridges a fundamental right; the Schedule was indeed inserted by the First Amendment, the legislature may still repeal or amend such an Act, and since the Coelho ruling these laws remain open to review on basic-structure grounds.

value: Only the first statement is correct
reasoning: Harappan streets followed a broadly grid-like plan but were not perfectly straight and did not everywhere meet at right angles. What was standardised in the brickwork was the proportion of length to breadth to thickness at four to two to one; the actual dimensions differed, larger bricks being used in fortification walls than in houses, so the sizes were not uniform between the two.

value: Kurinchi-mountainous, Palai-arid, Neytal-seashore, Mullai-pastoral
reasoning: The five landscapes of Sangam poetry name kurinchi as the hills, mullai as the pastoral woodland, marutam as the farmed plains, neytal as the coast and palai as the parched wasteland.

value: Only the third statement is incorrect
reasoning: Delimitation is governed by a Delimitation Act enacted by Parliament and carried out by a Delimitation Commission, so the Election Commission does not make those laws; preparation of the electoral rolls does rest with the Election Commission under Article 324, the Model Code takes effect the moment the schedule is announced, and Article 329 bars any challenge to an election except by election petition.

value: The claim that the Commission's reports are laid only before the Lok Sabha
reasoning: The Commission reports to the President, who causes the reports to be laid before each House of Parliament along with a memorandum explaining the action taken on the recommendations, so both Houses receive them, not the Lok Sabha alone.

value: A freedom guaranteed to citizens only
reasoning: The right to form associations or unions is one of the freedoms listed in Article 19(1), and every freedom in Article 19 is conferred on citizens alone, unlike Articles 14 and 21, which protect all persons.

value: By amending the First Schedule through Parliament's constituent amending power
reasoning: Since ceding Indian territory to a foreign state cannot be done by executive agreement or ordinary law, the exchange of enclaves under the Land Boundary Agreement was given effect by the Hundredth Constitutional Amendment of 2015, which altered the First Schedule using Parliament's amending power under Article 368; the First Schedule is not among the entrenched provisions requiring ratification by the State legislatures.
